Scan a project's submissions for prompt injection attempts

Source: R/injection-scan.R
scan_project.Rd

Looks through every student repository and rendered report for text aimed at an automated grader rather than at the instructor: instructions to ignore the rubric or award full marks, text addressed to an AI model, chat role markers, fabricated grading output, and above all text a human reader would not see (HTML comments, elements hidden by style or class, invisible Unicode characters, code in chunks that are not shown, base64, attribute and meta text in the rendered HTML, look-alike letters from other scripts). In rendered HTML it also reports active content: scripts that reach out of the report's frame or carry injection text, scripts loaded from an unusual host, event-handler attributes and outside frames. It also reports agent instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, ...) shipped in a repository and <!-- markermd: ... --> repair markers that were not added by the bundled markermd-fix-parsing skill.

Usage

scan_project(project = ".", artifacts = TRUE)

Arguments

project

Path to an initialized markermd project directory.

artifacts

Logical. Also scan the rendered HTML reports found under the project's configured artifacts directories (TRUE, the default).

Value

A data frame with one row per finding, ordered by repository and severity, with columns repo, source ("repo" or "artifact"), file (relative to the project root), line (NA for rendered HTML and file-level findings), severity, detector, matched and excerpt.

detector says where the text sits: visible-text, html-comment, hidden-style, hidden-chunk, hidden-element, html-attribute, invisible-unicode, bidi-control, look-alike-text, encoded-text, active-content, markermd-marker, agent-file or file-name. matched lists the content patterns it hit (instruction-override, grader-addressed, grade-demand, role-marker, grading-output, score-line, rubric-text), or NA. severity is "high" for a content match in a concealed place (and for smuggled Unicode, look-alike spelling and scripts that reach out of the report), "medium" for visible text matching two different content categories, an agent file, an event handler, a script from an unusual host or an unverified repair marker, and "low" for visible text matching one category, concealment with no content match, or an outside frame. excerpt is a single line, truncated, with invisible characters shown as <U+XXXX>.

Details

The scan is deterministic pattern matching and reads no file as instructions. It is meant to catch obvious attempts and to give a human (or the bundled markermd-check-injection skill) a short list to judge; it changes nothing in the project, and a finding is a candidate, not a verdict. Text inside images, persuasion written as ordinary prose, and heavier obfuscation are not detected.

Findings that also occur in the key repository are dropped, as are low and medium findings shared by more than half of the repositories (when there are at least four), since both are starter text rather than a student's doing.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res = scan_project("hw01")
res[res$severity == "high", ]
} # }
